sentences.text: The petitioner has filed his petition under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for enlarging him on bail in Crime No.168/2023 of Chikkanayakanahalli Police Station, Tumakuru District, registered for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC as well as Section 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ( for short, 'POCSO Act'), which is now pending on the file of the Additional Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, Tumakuru, in Spl.Case No.18/2024.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Heard arguments advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for the respondent-State.
Perused the records.
3. The allegation prosecution discloses that, the victim was studying in 10th Standard.
Once, the petitioner had gone to the house of victim when no other person was present in her house and has committed sexual intercourse with the victim.

It is further alleged that NC: 2024:KHC:15143 thereafter the petitioner used to repeatedly go to the house of the victim when she was alone and despite she closing the front door of her house, he used to get an access through back door and used to forcibly disrobe the victim and subject her to penetrative sexual assault.

It is alleged that in a year,
for 10 to 12 times he had committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl and he used to give her Rs.100/- every time and also asking her not to disclose the same to anybody.

It is further alleged that, subsequently when the victim had been to the house of other accused to pluck flowers, he has also committed penetrative sexual assault, which has resulted in her pregnancy.

The mother of the victim, who is the complainant, was unaware of all these aspects and only when the victim has complained pain in the abdomen, the complainant took her to the hospital and on examination, the victim was found to be pregnant and on an enquiry the victim has narrated the incident and hence,
the complainant has lodged a complaint in this regard.
On the basis of the complaint, the petitioner was arrested and NC: 2024:KHC:15143 was remanded to judicial custody.
The petitioner has approached the learned Special Judge seeking bail and his bail petition came to be rejected, and hence he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that, out of personal rivalry the said complaint is filed against him and there are lot of issues which cannot be expressed.
He would also assert that the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. do not tally with each other.
He would undertake to abide by all the terms and conditions to be imposed by this Court and prays for admitting the petitioner on bail.

5. Per contra the learned HCGP would seriously oppose the bail petition contending that, in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim has narrated the incident Mr Hemanth vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132996622/
2 in detail and there is prima facie material and the petitioner has exploited the helpless condition of the victim, and in case the petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:15143 is enlarged on bail, there is every possibility of he tampering the prosecution witnesses.

entities.text: Mr Hemanth vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it is evident that, the victim was minor being aged about 16 years when the present petitioner was alleged to have committed sexual assault on her.
The allegation clearly discloses that, she was regularly subjected to sexual assault by way of penetrative sexual intercourse by the petitioner and he used to pay Rs.100/- to her.
The allegations further disclose that, he used to enter the house of the victim from back door when the victim was alone in the house and used to exploit her helpless condition.

The medical report discloses that the victim was pregnant and though the FSL report does not disclose about tracing of seminal stains etc., the possibility of tracing of seminal stains is ruled-out since she was subjected to medical examination after long lapse of penetrative sexual assault and hence, tracing the seminal NC:
2024:KHC:15143 stains or other evidence in this regard
does not arise at all.
However, the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. clearly establish as to how she was exploited by the petitioner.
This is a serious offence and apart from that, the petitioner is aged about 30 years while the victim was aged about 16 to 17 years.
Since it is not a love affair, question of his false implication in this case does not arise at all.
7. Looking to the facts and circumstances and the seriousness as well as gravity of the offence, this is not a fit case wherein discretion can be exercised in favour of the petitioner.
Hence, the petition being devoid of any merits, does not survive for consideration and accordingly, the petition stands dismissed.

Sd/-
JUDGE KGR*
